title: Console MVP slice A: trim scope for dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown
creator: Aisha Malik
description: We must reduce the initial scope for Redwood Console (dashboards, distributed tracing, and cost breakdown) to hit an earlier Q2 release with limited engineering bandwidth and necessary backend infra changes. This ticket captures the approved scope cuts (Slice A), the acceptance criteria for the trimmed MVP, trade-offs, and the migration path for deferred features.
decisions: Ship a trimmed Dashboard surface focused on operational KPIs per-route and per-model; full customizable widgets are deferred to Slice B.
Tracing will be launched as sampled, high-level traces with span summary and a link to raw request logs; full span-by-span waterfall with long retention is deferred.
Cost breakdown will expose per-route and per-model aggregated costs with top-5 contributors and CSV export; per-token, per-user drilldowns and hourly rolling costs are deferred.
Data retention for the MVP will be 90 days for dashboards and traces (instead of the long-term 365d retention target) to avoid immediate storage/backfill work.

All hosted and Dedicated customers will get feature parity for the MVP surface; Private (on-prem) will be supported via a follow-up compatibility pass (Slice B) due to packaging and installer constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: provides three default panels for selected time range: total requests, p95 latency, and cost per 1k tokens, with time-range selector and ability to switch models/routes.
Dashboard: supports export of the currently selected view as CSV and basic date range comparisons (last period vs current).

Tracing: samples 1% of requests or up to 100 req/min per route, captures trace ID, top-level spans, duration, and error flag; each trace provides a deep link to the raw request log in the logs product (if available).
Cost breakdown: shows aggregated cost by route and by model for the selected window with top-5 contributors and a CSV export; numbers match billing report within 2% for the sample window.
Performance: dashboard queries respond within 2s for 95% of requests for common time ranges (1h, 24h, 7d).
RBAC: console users with existing read-only vs admin roles see appropriate gating for cost data; no new roles required for launch.
Telemetry: product analytics event emitted for user interaction with dashboards/traces/cost exports for later iteration and prioritization.
progress_notes: 2025-02-10: Drafted scope options after engineering capacity review; proposed Slice A to reduce backend changes (Aisha).
2025-02-12: Eng feedback (Marco Duarte): 90-day retention avoids immediate migration of cold storage; tracing sampling implementation fits current tracing pipeline.
2025-02-13: Design review (Nora Patel): default dashboard panels and CSV export UX mocked; recommended deferring widget library and custom layouts.
2025-02-14: Security sign-off for coarse-grained cost view confirmed; no additional KMS changes required for MVP (Jake, Security).
2025-02-17: Stakeholder review meeting: PMs, Eng leads, and Sales agreed on Slice A; noted enterprise customers may request per-user cost breakdown as expedited follow-up.
2025-02-18: Submitted for product leadership review and alignment with marketing launch cadence; documenting migration path for deferred features.
notes_for_engineering: Minimal backend schema changes only: add aggregated cost by route/model for 90d window, tracing sampling flag, and CSV export endpoints. Defer per-token aggregation pipeline and long-term retention index rebuild to Slice B. Engineering to provide rollback plan for high query load.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Enterprise customers may request per-user cost breakdown before Slice B; mitigation: include an FAQ and a sales-runbook with placeholders and a timeline. Risk: Query latency spikes for large orgs; mitigation: cap default time window to 7d on initial queries and offer async export for larger ranges.
open_questions: Should we permit admins to toggle tracing sampling rate per-organization at launch or postpone to Slice B? (Engineering leans postpone)
Do we need a temporary banner for customers that explains 90-day retention and the roadmap to 365d? (PM/Comms)
Are there any enterprise contracts requiring immediate per-user billing visibility that would block this MVP? (Sales to verify)
